title: Benchmark triage weekly rotation - Mar 18 2026
content:
Attendees: Sana, Miguel, Jia, Rohit, Eve

Purpose: weekly rotating triage of benchmark/latency anomalies and run validation. Focus this week: unusual P90 jumps observed in shadow runs and a throughput dip in dedicated pool alpha.

Summary of runs reviewed
- nightly-shadow-run (2026-03-17 03:20 UTC): model rw-chat-8b-q5, seq=1024, batch heuristic=adaptive, observed P50 48ms (baseline ~45ms), P90 126ms (baseline 78ms). Error rate stable (0.03%).
- dedicated-alpha-load-test (2026-03-17 09:10 UTC): sustained QPS 1.8k, target 2k; average tokens/sec down ~9% vs last week under same config.
- prefix-cache-eviction-sweep (2026-03-17 01:00 UTC): KV cache hit-rate dropped from 88% -> 64% on long-tail traffic shard B.

Immediate hypotheses
- KV cache temperature regression: eviction policy experiment from PR #3145 may have increased churn on smaller sequences; long-tail seqs are causing cache thrash and extra compute. (Owner: Jia)
- Batching heuristic interaction with autoscaler: adaptive batching + scale-down aggressiveness leads to transient smaller micro-batches causing per-token overhead to increase. (Owner: Rohit)
- Driver-side load generator mismatch: some load generators sent bursty client behavior (microbursts) that are not representative of production; need to replay production traces. (Owner: Miguel)

Data points pulled during meeting
- Flamegraphs: sample captures show additional GPU kernel scheduling gaps at 60-80ms intervals during P90 spikes. Suspect kernel preemption when tiny slices are scheduled.
- Trace snippets: slow traces show repeated KV lookups for identical prefixes (5x) instead of cached access; suggests cache key normalization bug in run-time.
- Autoscaler logs (dedicated-alpha): several scale-down events between 08:55-09:05 followed by immediate scale-ups -> correlated with throughput drop window.

Quick experiments to run (next 48h)
- Re-run nightly-shadow-run with KV cache forced to LRU (rollback PR #3145 changes) on subset (shard B) to verify hit-rate recovery. (Jia, due 2026-03-19)
- Replay 24h of production ingress from 2026-03-12 on dedicated-alpha with current autoscaler settings, then with conservative cool-down (scale-down delay +30s) to measure QPS continuity. (Miguel + SRE, due 2026-03-20)
- Short A/B microbench: disable adaptive batching for 1h on a canary pool to isolate batching impact on P90. Capture token/sec and P95. (Rohit, due 2026-03-19)
- Trace-level KV key normalization test: instrument code path to log normalized keys for slow requests. If keys differ due to whitespace/encoding, add quick fix to normalize. (Eve, due 2026-03-19)

Action items and owners
- Jia: run LRU rollback on shard B, gather hit-rate and latency delta, post results to #perf-triage. (2026-03-19)
- Rohit: schedule micro-A/B on canary pool, include spike generator and baseline generator, capture full pprof + nvprof. (2026-03-19)
- Miguel: coordinate replay with SRE and generate replay job; ensure secrets and customer data scrubbed before replay. (2026-03-20)
- Sana: open a short-lived investigation ticket (SERV-8921) to track root-cause artifacts and link all runs/PRs. Add owners and required artifacts. (done)
- Eve: add lightweight key-normalization logging to nightly debug build and gate it behind env var to avoid perf impact. (2026-03-19)

Decision notes
- No rollback to stable globally until shard-level validation passes. We will contain experiment to shard B and canary pool.
- Autoscaler cool-down tuning is cheap experiment and low risk; plan to test conservative delay before changing global policy.

Risks and open questions
- If KV normalization is the root cause, there may be other subtle caches (embedding cache, prefix index) with similar issues. We need to scan codepaths.
- If batching heuristic is primary, changing heuristics may alter cost/perf tradeoff; run cost simulation before broad rollout.

Artifacts to attach after experiments
- pprof tarballs, nvprof timelines, trace snippets (trace ids), KV hit-rate delta CSVs, autoscaler event logs. Link to confluence page 'bench/nightly-2026-03-17' for raw artifacts.

Next sync
- Quick async update in #perf-triage expected by EOD 2026-03-19 from each owner. Follow-up in triage meeting Mon 2026-03-22 09:30 PT to review artifacts and decide on rollback / roll-forward.

Notes / informal observations
- Miguel: saw oddness where client replay used 512-token truncation vs production 256 -> could influence cache temperature.
- Jia: thinks recent kernel scheduling tweak (kernel-scheduler-v2) might interact with very small micro-batches; might need a tiny scheduling window to coalesce.
- Rohit: suggests adding a short-run 'steady-state' test after scale events to validate autoscaler hysteresis.

Links referenced in discussion
- GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3145
- Ticket: SERV-8872 (KV eviction experiment)

End of notes.
